title: Release switchback sketchbook — anchor cohort & fast-fallback notes
content:
Notes to self — messy brain dump for a modular release pattern I want to try (switchback + anchor cohorts).

Date: 2024-07-18 (iterated 2024-09-02)
Context: frequent small model variant pushes make full traffic cutovers risky for low-latency products. Need a lightweight approach that:
- lets us validate user-facing behaviour at 1–5% quickly
- allows fast automated rollback to a known-good variant (switchback) without expensive state rebuilds
- keeps KV cache warm enough to avoid cold-latency spikes for cohorts

Primary idea (sketch):
1) Anchor cohort: select small set of always-on clients (internal + a few external beta tenants) that get pinned to the new variant for longer (days). Purpose: long-running signal on quality regressions, memory/kv stability.
2) Staggered public canary: start 0.5% -> 2% -> 5% over a few hours. Between steps, run auto-checks and manual eyeballs.
3) Switchback window: maintain previous variant in warm standby with KV hotness preserved (mirrored caches if possible). If a regression triggers, immediately flip traffic back and keep the candidate pinned to anchor cohort for postmortem.

Operational checklist (first-run runbook):
- Preflight (T-24h): merge PR, bake artifacts to staging; run unit/infra checks (build OK, image size, quantization table). Notify #deploy-ops.
- Warmup (T-2h): ramp a small warmup cohort (internal bots + synthetic traffic) to seed caches and measure 95/99 latency.
- Start (T0): open 0.5% traffic, leave for minimum 30m stable window. Export metric snapshot (latency, error rate, token cost) to release bucket.
- Grow: 0.5% -> 2% (30–60m) -> 5% (1–2h). At each step run gating checks.
- Anchor pin: ensure anchor cohort (IDs below) are pinned to candidate full-time for at least 72h.

Anchor cohort (initial):
- service:internal-batch-test, tenant:beta-acme, tenant:platform-experiments
- NOTE: pick internal clients that exercise long context paths + unusual tokenization edge cases.

Gating checks (automated):
- 95th/99th latency compared to baseline: delta <= +20%
- error rate (HTTP 5xx or generation aborts) <= baseline + 0.1% absolute
- hallucination proxy (BLEU / similarity on seeded prompts) no drop > 3%
- cost-per-token not exceed baseline by > 10% (quantization or kernel change oversight)
- tail token spend anomaly detection (sudden spike in average tokens per request)

Manual checks:
- quick manual review of samples from anchor cohort (we log seeded prompt set + random queries)
- check console traces for KV eviction spikes and backend GPU memory churn
- sanity check on regression alerts from Redwood Optimize monitoring (if present)

Rollback / Switchback logic:
- Trigger conditions: any automated gating fail OR SRE/PM manual veto.
- Procedure: flip traffic routing rule to previous variant (warm standby routing) and hold for 30m.
- Post-switchback instrument: annotate timeline in incident doc, pin candidate to anchor cohort, add experiment label to model metadata.
- Fast cleanup: throttle new candidate’s rollout, run deeper model evals, collect failure cases.

Cache + KV considerations:
- Warm standby approach: maintain an in-memory mirror of KV caches for the previous variant where feasible. If not possible, deploy candidate with KV prefix mapping so candidate can reuse cached prefixes from previous variant for identical prefix hashes.
- Synthetic warmers: deploy a scheduled bot that replays high-frequency prefixes during warmup windows to prime KV. Avoid hitting rate-limits.

Traffic routing implementation notes (practical):
- Use routing tags: variant:v2, fallback:v1, cohort:anchor. Route by percentage via traffic-layer config; ensure config change is small (single click + API).
- Rolling routing changes by region first (na-west-1 -> eu-west-1) can reduce blast radius but complicates metrics normalization. Start same-time cross-region for simplicity on first run.

Telemetry to capture (minimum):
- model_variant, request_id, tenant_id, route_tag, latency_p50_p95_p99, token_count, error_code, kv_hit_rate (if instrumented), gpu_memory_mb_at_call
- special: sample of model outputs (anonymized) for anchor cohort (for manual triage)

Questions / unknowns to resolve (TODO):
- How to cheaply maintain mirrored KV for multi-variant runtime? (action: talk to infra infra/kv folks)
- Exact anchor cohort membership — need approvals for using any customer tenant as anchor (action: ping CS for consent)
- How to automate switchback (API vs manual) and safe-guard accidental flaps? Add a cooldown window?

Quick CLI snippets (notes):
# list routing rules
redwoodctl routing list --model my-model --env prod
# set traffic split to 0.5%
redwoodctl routing set --model my-model --split v2=0.005 --reason "switchback experiment 2024-07-18"

Postmortem capture fields (if roll back happens):
- hypothesis, detection time, who flipped, root-cause (perf/regression/infra), reproduction steps, mitigation, follow-up actions, owners.

Follow-up experiments to codify:
- automated anchor cohort: script that rotates internal clients and generates synthetic long-context traffic daily
- metric-driven switchback: if 95p latency breach persists for >2 consecutive windows, auto-flip back with operator notification
- capacity hedging: keep 10% headroom on standby GPUs for fast switchback

Misc notes (random):
- anchor cohorts are powerful — they catch slow regressions that brief canaries miss (think memory leakage, gradual drift). Need a playbook that keeps them small and private.
- try not to overload CS/SE with anchor-only incidents; keep them informed and give opt-out.

Next steps (short):
1) run prototype on staging this week (Arjun owns infra changes).
2) loop in CS about anchor tenants (Lina to check permissions).
3) draft a short runbook and post in #deploy-ops.

End of sketchbook — will refine after staging run.

Unresolved: where to persist anchor cohort list so it's auditable and not in one user's doc? Probably product-hosted-api/confluence page + a tiny ACL record in the console config.

-- N.P.
